newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen vows to protect tourists from kidnappers.
newsitem.headline: Yemen vows to protect tourists from kidnappers.

text.p: Yemen has launched a campaign to protect Western tourists against kidnapping by local tribesmen, a weekly newspaper said on Wednesday.

"The interior ministry and concerned authorities are currently undertaking security arrangements to curb the phenomenon of kidnapping foreigners and to ensure they are not repeated again," Abdul-Rahman al-Mahyoub, head of the country's tourism authority, told al-Wahda Arabic weekly.
He gave no further details and officials were not available for comment.

Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats and other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips. All have been freed unharmed.
Mahyoub said he expected one million Arab and foreign tourists to visit Yemen over the next five years.
Seven German tourists were freed earlier this month after being held hostage by Yemeni tribesmen for nine days.

Some 75,000 people visited Yemen in 1996, up 20 percent from 1995, official figures show. Tourism revenues in Yemen, one of the Arab world's most impoverished countries, rose to $75-80 million from about $30 million the previous year.
